body:
As far as I was able to test it, it seems it slows down more due to the sheer amount of Nodes in the scene. Even if you remove `EditorNode::update_resource_count` call from `SceneTreeEditor::_update_node_subtree`, it's still considerably slower than 4.5 (though the freeze was still there)

However, emitting the signal indiscriminately causes Godot to almost crash on my machine, so It's definitely related to a loss in performance.  Adding a check here seems appropriate.
Can you check again in beta2? It should be better.

I can confirm this on 4.7.beta 860821708 when editing Extra Spacing while `scene_1` is the current scene tab:

> Godot v4.7.beta (860821708) - Fedora Linux 44 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (nvidia; 595.71.05) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 62.33 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

I could also reproduce this on 4.7.beta1 and 4.7.beta2 official builds. I bisected the regression to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109458.

This has nothing to do with changing the parameters. The editor hangs because the font resource picker is in the tree and it's spammed with update requests (which are expensive due to resource preview stuff). Restarting the project clears the inspector, so the theme is no longer edited, so there is no resource picker to update.
